clue.text: When separating what's due, car (new) might be part of this?

indicators.note: being part of something means sitting within it, so these pieces go inside the outer word

parts.note: what is due to you for work is your pay; it splits to take the inner pieces
a limo, short for limousine, is a large car
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A separating couple wrangle over what each is owed, and a brand-new car might be part of the settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What’s due' does double duty: it is PAY in the wordplay and also part of the definition. PA(LIMO N)Y gives PALIMONY.
explanation.definitionFit: Palimony is the financial support claimed by an unmarried partner after a couple split up, so it is money owed at separation.

clue.text: Sanction America's border fences

indicators.note: a fence encloses something, so the words around it hold the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: The USA punishes people by building barriers along its frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a court order restricting someone's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anti-Social Behaviour Order was a legal penalty imposed by British courts, so it is a kind of official punishment.

clue.text: Slip gets by two people at least

parts.note: a runner who laps another goes past them
'us' means the speaker plus at least one other person

explanation.surface: Someone slips past a couple of people on a crowded path.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as LAPS US, the answer means 'gets by at least two people'. 'Slip' looks like a verb in the surface but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapsus is a Latin word used in English for an error or blunder, as in lapsus linguae, a slip of the tongue.

clue.text: 'Cigar' Marx brother cut banker up

indicators.note: cutting something shortens it, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Zeppo was the youngest Marx brother; his name loses its final letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a banker is a river, something with banks; here the Nile

explanation.surface: Groucho-style comedy: a Marx brother with his famous cigar, cutting a banker down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword favourite for a river. The quotation marks around 'Cigar' show it is a nickname: a cigar-shaped airship.
explanation.definitionFit: A zeppelin is a rigid airship whose long rounded body resembles a cigar, hence the playful description.

clue.text: Dr. Spooner's to manoeuvre uterus with this scope

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version swaps them here

parts.note: to manoeuvre is to wriggle; it takes the other word's opening W sound in exchange for its own R
the uterus is the womb; it takes the R sound in exchange for its W

explanation.surface: A comic image of the bumbling clergyman trying to steer a womb with a medical scope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scope' looks like a medical instrument such as an endoscope; it is the definition, meaning latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiggle room is informal for leeway or freedom to adjust, which is one sense of scope.

clue.text: Dodge weekly costs of theatre production

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a way of escaping an obligation
second meaning: a theatre term for the weekly running expenses of a show

explanation.walkthrough: The theatrical sense is obscure but in Chambers; most solvers will know only the escape-clause meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-out is an excuse or loophole for avoiding something, and in theatre jargon also the sum a show must take each week to cover expenses.

clue.text: Heading to Norway, relative crosses ocean — does this make her sick?

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the country

indicators.note: to cross something here is to straddle it, so one piece spans the other

parts.note: an aunt is a relative; she opens to take the next piece
an ocean is a sea

explanation.surface: An aunt sets off across the North Sea to Norway, and one wonders whether the voyage will make her seasick.
explanation.walkthrough: The aunt in the wordplay is the 'her' of the definition, so the clue reads as one story.
explanation.definitionFit: A nauseant is a substance or agent that induces nausea, so it is what would make someone feel sick.

clue.text: Final one-two from Roy's team was successful

indicators.note: the final one letter is taken from one word and the final two from the other

parts.note: Roy of the Rovers was a British comic-strip footballer who played for Melchester Rovers

explanation.surface: Roy's football side won with a slick one-two pass in the final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final one-two' sounds like a passing move in a cup final; it means lose the last letter of THE and the last two of ROVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Throve is an older past tense of thrive, and to thrive is to prosper or flourish.

clue.text: Adele's last exploit with male rapper

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the singer's name
to exploit a resource is to mine it
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Adele's latest venture is a collaboration with a male rap star.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface steers toward music business; 'exploit' is a verb here, not a noun meaning a feat.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminem is the stage name of the American hip-hop artist Marshall Mathers, so he is a famous example of a rapper.

clue.text: High priest out of opera used as setter's name?

indicators.note: taking something out of a word removes those letters from it

parts.note: Fidelio is Beethoven's only opera
Eli is the Old Testament priest, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A high priest has been dropped from an opera's cast, and the crossword compiler borrows the name.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is not the compiler but a dog: an Irish or English setter could be called Fido.
explanation.definitionFit: Fido is the stock name for a pet dog, and a setter is a gun-dog breed, so it is a plausible name for one.

clue.text: Needing change, Scrooge regularly tapped another old miser

indicators.note: a change rearranges something, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Short of loose change, Scrooge keeps borrowing from another skinflint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' sounds like coins, fitting the miser story; it is the signal to rearrange. Scrooge is Dickens's miser, hence 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapegood is an archaic word for a stingy hoarder, someone who scrapes together every penny.

clue.text: House dismisses frauds

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
to axe someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: A firm, or the House of Commons, sacks its cheats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House dismisses' reads like a sentence with a subject and verb; in fact both words are pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoaxes are deceptions or tricks meant to fool people, so they are frauds in the sense of swindles.

clue.text: Co-ordinates playing of Chopin to hide look of instrument

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: x and y are the two coordinates on a graph

indicators.note: playing a piece interprets it freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A pianist plays Chopin in a way that disguises what instrument it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's name and LO go into the mix together; X and Y are the familiar graph axes.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylophonic is the adjective for the xylophone, the percussion instrument of tuned wooden bars.

clue.text: All for end in blood-feud in island capital

indicators.note: one thing for another means it takes the other's place

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed
a vendetta is a long-running blood feud

explanation.surface: Everyone wants an end to the island's blood feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' is not a signal to take a last letter; it is the literal word swapped out of VENDETTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Valletta is the capital city of Malta, the Mediterranean island nation.

clue.text: What's needed to convert Tory into Green?

definitions.text: What's needed to convert Tory into Green?

parts.words: What's needed to convert Tory into Green?
parts.note: surface reading: persuading a Conservative to join the Green Party
setter's reading: Tory blue is a colour, and mixing in a certain paint turns blue to green

explanation.surface: A political strategist wonders how to win a Conservative over to environmental politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory stands for blue, the Conservative party colour. In paint, blue plus the right primary makes green.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixing this primary colour with blue produces green, so it is the colour required to turn blue paint green.

clue.text: Canadian needing cop to replace Scot shooting well

indicators.note: replacing means putting one thing in another's place

parts.note: someone from the province of Ontario
to cop something is to get or catch it
Ian is a typically Scottish first name; these letters go out

explanation.surface: A Canadian marksman wants a policeman to stand in for a Scottish shooter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cop' looks like a police officer; it is the verb, meaning get.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot that is on target hits what it is aimed at, so a marksman on target is shooting accurately.

clue.text: With it, rhubarb's dry and unusable

parts.note: to be with it is to be in, fashionable
rhubarb belongs to the dock family of plants

explanation.surface: Garden talk: once harvested, rhubarb goes dry and inedible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' reads as 'along with it'; it means trendy. The 's of 'rhubarb's' stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship in dock is out of the water, often in dry dock for repairs, and so out of service meanwhile.

clue.text: Trusty scout makes off with OBE

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or awry, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: the British honour

explanation.surface: A reliable Scout leader runs off with an honour from the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Lone Ranger, Tonto calls the Ranger by this name, usually glossed as 'trusty scout' or 'faithful friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name Tonto uses for the Lone Ranger is traditionally said to mean faithful friend or trusty scout.

clue.text: Norman's best friend's classes tucked into Shakespeare

indicators.note: tucking something into another puts it inside

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard
RI is religious instruction, school classes

explanation.surface: A man called Norman's best friend has lessons in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman means a native of Normandy, not a man's name, and a dog is man's best friend: a French breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The briard is a large French sheepdog, so it is a dog, the proverbial best friend, from northern France.

clue.text: Cool dude with question for hard gag man

indicators.note: one thing for another means it takes the other's place

parts.note: a hipster is a trendy, cool person
QU is the abbreviation for question
H for hard, as on pencils; this letter goes out

explanation.surface: A trendy guy has a question for a tough comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard gag man' looks like one phrase; 'hard' belongs to the wordplay and 'gag man' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A quipster is someone who makes witty remarks, so a joke-teller, which is what a gag man is.

clue.text: You said redesigned patio could be perfect location

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is represented by a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter's name is pronounced the same as the pronoun

indicators.note: redesigning remakes something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden designer is told a new terrace would make a lovely spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'You said' is not a quotation tag but a letter that sounds like 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia, from Thomas More's book, is an imagined ideal place where everything is flawless.

clue.text: Announced prize: the setter is second to Harry Potter's duck!

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a gem is a prized thing; the sound is respelt
the setter refers to himself, so 'the setter is' becomes I'M

indicators.note: second means the letter in position two of the word

parts.note: the second letter of the name

explanation.surface: A quiz-show prize announcement: the setter comes second only to Harry Potter's pet duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry Potter' is split: Harry gives a letter, and Potter is Beatrix Potter, whose Jemima Puddle-Duck is a children's book heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Jemima Puddle-Duck is the farmyard duck in Beatrix Potter's children's tales.

clue.text: Traveller's ill feeling let out in car

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: Jag is informal for a Jaguar car

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A motion-sick traveller's nausea finally escapes during a car ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' looks like one phrasal verb; 'let' is the material and 'out' the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet lag is the tiredness and disorientation felt after long flights across time zones, an affliction of travellers.

clue.text: Look of gloom amongst company fleet not running

indicators.note: amongst means surrounded by, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
to lour is to frown or scowl; a lour is a sullen look
fleet means swift

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood hangs over a firm whose vehicle fleet is off the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' is the adjective, not a set of vehicles, and 'not running' is about dye, not engines.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourfast fabric keeps its dye in the wash, so its colours do not bleed or run.

clue.text: File that's fit for Fife's fools?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a coarse file for shaping wood or metal
second meaning: the Scots word for a raspberry, a fruit used in fools, the creamy desserts

explanation.walkthrough: Fife is a Scottish county; a fool is a whipped-cream fruit pudding, not a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a rough metal tool for smoothing surfaces, and in Scotland it is the usual word for a raspberry.

clue.text: Attic possibly has roof blown off, creating stink

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Attic is a dialect of ancient Greek, an example of it

explanation.surface: A loft whose roof has been blown away starts to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' looks like a loft, fitting 'roof'; with its capital it is the ancient Athenian form of a language.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to smell strongly and unpleasantly, which is what stinking means.

clue.text: — is under-sized fool in nonspeaking role?

definitions.text: — is under-sized fool in nonspeaking role?

indicators.note: something undersized falls short, so the word loses its last letter
in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a mime is a silent performance; it opens to take the inner piece
a nit is a fool, cut short by one letter

explanation.surface: The dash stands for the answer: a pocket-sized clown who never speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the dash as the answer's name and the whole clue describes the character; the same words build it as MI(NI)ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini-Me is the tiny, mute clone of Dr Evil in the Austin Powers films, a small comic sidekick who never talks.

clue.text: How liberated woman, after taking winter off, might reappear again and again?

indicators.note: liberated letters are set free from their order, so they are rearranged
taking letters off a word removes them from it
off means removed, completing the instruction to subtract

parts.note: the whole phrase is used as material, the first word included
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A free-spirited woman, shaking off the winter, keeps popping up again.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive anagram: strike WINTER's letters from LIBERATED WOMAN and rearrange the rest. Dame Nellie Melba, the Australian soprano, made farewell tour after farewell tour.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a Melba is a British and Australian idiom for repeatedly announcing retirement and then returning to perform.
